basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: A case is the accountable record of one request, issue or complaint from intake to closure.
Holds case-local communication and commitments applied to it, while SLA policies and calendars live elsewhere.
Differs from a work order or task, which carry out work the case may need.
Can be reopened under the same identity, unlike a new case about a similar matter.

may: Open a case from an inquiry with classification, requester and channel.
Propose triage, priority and assignment based on published rules.
Draft replies and summaries for the case owner.
Link related cases, incidents and work orders.
mustNot: Close a case as resolved without the requester's confirmation where the policy requires it.
Downgrade priority or reclassify a complaint to avoid an SLA breach.
Expose one requester's data to another in shared or linked cases.
Promise remedies or compensation not authorized by policy.
Delete case communication that is part of the record.
requiresHuman: Handling cases that involve safety, legal threats or vulnerable people.
Escalating to an external ombudsman or regulator.

considerations: Requesters may be in distress; responses should be respectful and not deflect with automation.
Case records hold personal data and should be kept only as long as needed.
Triage rules can treat customer groups unequally without anyone noticing.
affectedParties: Third parties named in case communication

items: A case has a case number, a requester, a classification, a state, an assignee and a communication history.
It is confused with an incident record, a work order and a single email thread.
Requests lost between queues without an owner.
Personal data disclosed to the wrong requester.
SLA breaches hidden by status manipulation.
Repeated complaints not linked, so a systemic fault is missed.
ITIL incident and service request practices.
Open311 GeoReport v2 for civic service requests.
